incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-8847 latency.outlier.proxy-usw2 - 3 nodes above 99th pct threshold
maria: @oncall-sre saw the page, pulling traces and logs now :eyes:
tony: acked (tony) - looking at routing/proxy layer, can anyone check autoscaler events?
priya: checking synthetics and customer error rates - quick glance looks like 200s, no spike in 5xx
oncall-sre: seeing a ~40s p99 spike starting 2026-03-15T15:02:10Z across router-3/7, p50 also nudged up then returned
maria: logs from router-7 around spike:
```
2026-03-15T15:02:11Z proxy[router-7]: req=zz12 backend=kv-node latency=3120ms status=200
2026-03-15T15:02:12Z proxy[router-3]: req=yy99 backend=ml-runtime latency=2950ms status=200
```
ops-runner: kubectl top pods --ns=runtime shows cpu stable, mem slight increase on router-7, net normal
tony: looks like KV cache cold misses + a tiny autoscaler bounce (scale up then back down) -> backend latencies spike but no errors
priya: verified real customer requests: no timeouts or retries, mobile and web telemetry show normal success rates
oncall-sre: PD will autoclear if duration below threshold — keep thread open to confirm no follow-ups
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-8847 auto-resolved after 52s
ops-runner: filing follow-up INF-641 to tune pre-warm and autoscaler hysteresis, attaching traces
maria: linking dash/traces: https://prom.example.com/d/xyz/proxy-latency and https://traces.example.com/t/abcd-1234
priya: recommend mark as no-customer-impact, post-incident label: transient, follow-up needed for pre-warm rules :memo:
tony: +1, add timeline note: transient KV warmup + autoscaler thrash, no 5xxs
oncall-sre: i'll watch the next 30m and escalate if it reappears, leaving monitoring hook on :thumbsup:
